# Lighting and MDL fixtures

The sixteen light stages use distinct architectural, sculptural and tabletop subjects with matte, metallic and translucent Preview Surface materials. They exercise rectangle, disk, cylinder, sphere, shaped spotlight, distant, animated and dome lights, color temperature and normalization, complete light-rig variants (`warmStudio`, `coolRim`, `nightNeon`), and environment variants (`day`, `night`, `dayRotated`). They also author a dome portal, mesh and volume light APIs, deprecated GeometryLight, light and shadow collections, and a cached light list. Those latter features require delegate-specific transport or linking support; the EXR dome or a separate key provides their visible illumination. The manifest requests no viewer-supplied environment or thumbnail camera light for these cases. The 64×32 Radiance RGBE maps and uncompressed linear OpenEXR map are original procedural assets with asymmetric bright areas. Native schema assertions establish the authored rig and resolved assets; they do not establish exact physical illumination or variant behavior. The current viewer approximates disk lights with rectangular area lights and cylinder lights with point lights. Plugin lights and filters require an external renderer-specific definition and are not represented.

The six MDL stages have MDL-only surface terminals and exercise the viewer's existing authored-input approximation for `OmniPBR`, its clearcoat and opacity variants, and `gltf_material`. The subjects include metal, clearcoat, color texture, normal texture, and cutout cases. The included `.mdl` files are the unmodified NVIDIA material implementations with their full import dependency closure, BSD licenses and hashes in `mdl-sources.json`. All six have native RTX scene references and MDL SDK material probes. Native Storm has no MDL renderer in this setup, so the existing Storm cards still show geometric display-color fallback. These six fixtures focus on OmniPBR and glTF inputs; they do not cover OmniGlass.

The generator writes an ignored local `native-validation.json` report with stage opens, composition errors and authored feature assertions with OpenUSD 26.05. The sixteen light stages also pass this build's `usdchecker`. The VolumeLight card uses `scripts/render-volume-light-reference.py` to render the surrounding native scene with the VDB volume deactivated in a temporary layer, because this Storm build lacks a VDB plugin; the card does not show volume emission. Its six MDL checks report `MissingSourceTypeInRegistry` because that OpenUSD installation has no MDL shader registry plugin; the separate RTX/SDK renders establish actual MDL execution. HDR, EXR and PNG dependencies are generated locally; NVIDIA MDL sources are preserved and checksum-verified by the generator.

Regenerate with:

```sh
python3 scripts/generate-lighting-mdl-fixtures.py
```

The torus meshes have analytic unit vertex normals on a 96×32 mesh, preserving smooth metal highlights. Native Storm cards use the same geometry. Distant sun also authors `UsdLuxShadowAPI` and an enabled/disabled `shadows` variant; both public viewers update actual shadow maps when it changes. Shadow color, distance/falloff and selective shadow-link collections remain separate renderer work.

Torus UVs use face-varying coordinates at both periodic seams. Geometric vertices and their analytic normals remain shared; each closing face reaches UV 1 instead of interpolating across the texture back to 0. The native UV regression checks every generated torus, and the browser regression checks the loaded MDL normal map and triangle UV spans in both viewers. This fixes the narrow distorted strips in `mdl-normal-texture`.

Native RTX scene references are available for [metal](references/mdl-metal.png), [clearcoat](references/mdl-clearcoat.png), [color texture](references/mdl-color-texture.png), [normal texture](references/mdl-normal-texture.png), [cutout opacity](references/mdl-opacity-mask.png) and [glTF](references/mdl-gltf.png). The reference manifest records image hashes and display settings; full capture logs remain in the local cache. The PNGs use Needle AgX, exposure 1 and sRGB. Commands for SSH scene rendering and local Mac material probes are in [Native MDL references](../../../../../docs/mdl-reference-rendering.md).

Every material has an `effect` variant on `/World/Looks/MDL`: `enabled` and `disabled` preserve geometry, camera and lighting while changing the demonstrated parameter. The native reference pairs use 256 samples and include `*-disabled.png` controls; the manifest records image differences within the central subject region. The normal case now uses a broad, normalized 512² tangent-space pillow relief on a flat panel, torus and explicitly UV-mapped spheres. Its [disabled control](references/mdl-normal-texture-disabled.png) sets only bump strength to zero. Clearcoat uses a rough base to make the smooth coat visible. Color tiles and circular perforations are deliberately large enough to inspect without zooming. All MDL sample spheres have authored UVs and smooth normals, avoiding renderer-dependent implicit sphere parameterization.

The light catalog uses `scenePrimitiveLightIntensityScale: 1`: authored luminance is no longer multiplied by different brightness overrides for each fixture. The delegate converts sphere luminance to point-light intensity, distant luminance to illuminance using the angular diameter, and normalized emission using world-space surface area. Disk lights retain a rectangular LTC approximation with matching total power; cylinders retain an isotropic point approximation. Nonuniformly scaled spheres use an effective radius rather than an ellipsoidal emitter. Native Storm 26.05 uses older projected-area normalization and point approximations for area lights, so its thumbnails are not an exact photometric reference for modern UsdLux normalization. Its display transform also differs from Needle AgX.

Preview Surface `emissiveColor` remains scene-linear and can exceed 1. Beauty applies ambient occlusion to reflected light without dimming emission. Optional bloom is available in View settings for the Three viewer's Basic and Beauty modes; it processes the HDR composite before tone mapping and includes transparent surfaces and volumes.
